title: Prismchime Ring
status: core + cabinet + 9 iterations merged on main; dossier is iteration 10
summary: A ring of crystal chimes hangs in the Prismheart. Tap a chime and its charge pulses along its facing, one chime per point, and the rung chime gains one from the resonance. A chime that fills to four peals: it scores, lights, resets and pushes one charge to each neighbour, so peals chain around the ring. Light every chime before the taps run out. Deterministic per seed, bit-exact between the Python rules, the C++ core and the Unreal cabinet.

mechanics.name: Ring
mechanics.text: 6 / 8 / 10 chimes (easy / normal / hard), each with a seeded starting charge of 1 or 2 and a facing (clockwise or counter). Only randrange is drawn; nothing random happens after the ring is hung.

mechanics.name: Tap
mechanics.text: Spends one tap. The chime sends one pulse to each of the next charge chimes in its facing (+1 each) and then gains one itself. Charge is never spent by tapping; taps inject energy.

mechanics.name: Peal
mechanics.text: A chime reaching 4 peals: +5 score, it lights, resets to 0 and gives +1 to both neighbours. Peals resolve in the order chimes filled (FIFO); a chime drained by a neighbour's peal before its turn does not peal. Excess above 4 is lost, which rewards exact fills.

mechanics.name: Win / loss
mechanics.text: Every chime lit (each has pealed at least once) wins and adds +3 per tap left. The last tap without a full ring loses. Score = 5 x peals (+ bonus).

mechanics.name: Budget
mechanics.text: 8 taps on every difficulty; difficulty is ring size. Greedy watcher win rate is pinned by test: easy 88-100 %, normal 70-95 %, hard 50-85 %; no one-tap wins.

mechanics.name: Guide (option 1)
mechanics.text: Practice mode: a blue ring marks the chime the watcher would tap (most newly lit, then most score, then lowest index) and the hint previews the cursor chime's peals and newly lit count.

mechanics.name: Saves
mechanics.text: Text save (shared DaedalusDesktopSaveText shape): difficulty, seed, taps, peals, score, over, won, cursor, charge, facing, lit. Range-checked on restore; charges must be below 4, facings +1/-1, lit mask the ring's length.

mechanics.name: Controls
mechanics.text: Left/Right or stick walk the ring; A / J / Space tap; R or pad Start restart a finished ring. Cabinet class DesktopGames/DaedalusDesktopPrismchimeCore.h, registry id prismchime, save slot prismchime.dgs.

items.text: An unlit crystal bell on a silver rod; charge shows as 0-3 glowing pips stacked inside the bell.
The same bell after its first peal: warm amber glass, a faint hum; pips turn to dark brass.
A small sky-blue arrowhead on the ring tangent beside each chime, pointing the way its pulses travel.
The silver hoop the chimes hang from, two concentric rings with the bells between.
A short prism-headed mallet; the cursor's gold ring is where it hovers.
A burst of light when a chime peals, with two sparks leaving to the neighbours.

storyline.text: In the Prismheart's inner court a ring of chimes has fallen silent. The Wardens say the court only opens its deeper doors when every chime has rung once in a single vigil.
A Warden shows the first tap: charge runs the way the arrow points, and a chime brimming with four pulses sings and wakes its neighbours. (The tutorial rows appear only on a fresh ring.)
Each difficulty is a wider court: six chimes, then eight, then ten, with the same eight taps. The player learns to set up chains rather than ring the loudest chime.
A full ring: every chime lit before the taps run out. The leftover taps become the Wardens' gratitude (+3 each).
The ring falls silent and the court stays shut; pad A or R hangs a new ring at the same seed, so the pattern can be studied and beaten.
The chime ring is a side-court puzzle next to the Glimmerloom market; it does not gate the main campaign but lit rings add to the arcade scoreboard like the other Prismheart cabinets.
